import logging

def test_caplog_consistency_after_clear(caplog):
    """Test that caplog.get_records and caplog.records stay consistent after clear."""
    # Initially empty
    assert caplog.get_records("call") == caplog.records == []
    
    # Add a log record
    logging.warning("test message 1")
    assert len(caplog.get_records("call")) == 1
    assert len(caplog.records) == 1
    assert caplog.get_records("call") == caplog.records
    
    # Clear and verify both are empty
    caplog.clear()
    assert caplog.get_records("call") == caplog.records == []
    
    # Add another record after clear
    logging.error("test message 2")
    assert len(caplog.get_records("call")) == 1
    assert len(caplog.records) == 1
    assert caplog.get_records("call") == caplog.records
    assert caplog.records[0].getMessage() == "test message 2"

def test_multiple_clears(caplog):
    """Test multiple clear operations."""
    logging.warning("message 1")  # Use WARNING level to ensure it's captured
    assert len(caplog.records) == 1
    
    caplog.clear()
    assert len(caplog.records) == 0
    assert len(caplog.get_records("call")) == 0
    
    logging.warning("message 2")
    assert len(caplog.records) == 1
    
    caplog.clear()
    assert len(caplog.records) == 0
    assert len(caplog.get_records("call")) == 0

def test_caplog_text_after_clear(caplog):
    """Test that caplog.text is also cleared properly."""
    logging.warning("test message")
    assert "test message" in caplog.text
    assert len(caplog.records) == 1
    
    caplog.clear()
    assert caplog.text == ""
    assert len(caplog.records) == 0
    assert len(caplog.get_records("call")) == 0

def test_clear_preserves_identity(caplog):
    """Test that clear preserves the identity relationship between get_records and records."""
    logging.warning("test")
    records_before = caplog.get_records("call")
    handler_records_before = caplog.records
    
    # They should be the same object initially
    assert records_before is handler_records_before
    
    caplog.clear()
    
    records_after = caplog.get_records("call")
    handler_records_after = caplog.records
    
    # After clear, they should still be the same object (both pointing to the new empty list)
    assert records_after is handler_records_after
    assert records_after == handler_records_after == []

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import pytest
    pytest.main([__file__, "-v"])
